summary: Retested the Drive integration regression: public API and all sampled protected routes behave correctly, the frontend builds, the Google sign-in screen redirects to Emergent/Google, invalid session callbacks recover, and mobile auth has no horizontal overflow. Real Google OAuth callback, authenticated dashboard, Drive authorization, upload, AI streaming, and logout could not be completed without a configured test identity.

minor.issue: Callback persists client_secret in drive_credentials; credentials are not returned by the tested API responses, but plaintext-at-rest storage is a security concern and remains in the PRD backlog.

integration_issues.flow: Authenticated Drive settings and file/AI flows
integration_issues.issue: Blocked from end-to-end execution because no Google test identity is available; unauthenticated guards were verified as 401.

action_items: Run a real Google test identity through Emergent login, then connect Drive from Settings and verify callback, status, and folder authorization.
After OAuth, test authenticated dashboard/navigation, odontogram persistence, anonymous image upload, AI SSE response, and logout.
Avoid persisting Google client secrets in plaintext and use a required environment-provided frontend callback URL rather than a hardcoded fallback.
critical_code_review_comments: drive_callback stores client_secret in MongoDB; encrypt or avoid storing the secret at rest before production use.

SimplePage connectDrive has no catch/error state, so a failed authenticated Drive-connect request can leave the user without actionable feedback; the upload and AI flows similarly lack visible request-error handling.

success_rate.backend: 100% (7/7 regression tests passed; unauthenticated Drive/storage/AI probes also returned expected 401)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of executable unauthenticated/mobile checks passed; authenticated flows blocked

context_for_next_testing_agent: Public /api/ returns 200; /api/auth/me, dashboard, patients, calendar, library, inventory, Drive connect/status, files, and AI stream reject unauthenticated requests with 401. Google sign-in redirects to accounts.google.com, invalid #session_id callback clears the hash, and 390px auth has no overflow. Use a configured Google test identity to finish authenticated OAuth/Drive and logout coverage.
rca of the issue: The prior current_user Header-sentinel regression is fixed in the live service: direct protected route calls now enter the intended no-token branch and return 401. Remaining coverage is environment-blocked rather than a reproduced application failure.
